title: Co-cultivation Protocol for Porosira glacialis Diatom and Bacterial Isolates
author: William Arnli
materials: From the 0.25 millimolar (mM) 1H-Indole-3-acetic acid, 98% Thermo Scientific (CAS: 87-51-4) stock spike 100 µL of IAA to each of the IAA treatment culture flasks to achieve a final concentration of 50 nanomolar (nM) . Immediately proceed to step 16.

steps.title: Set up shaker and lighting
steps.instruction: Position a large orbital shaker in a 7 °C cold‑room and install flexible 200 × 50 W RGB LED strips along the shaker to provide sufficient cultivation light. Use the PSU‑20i Orbital Shaking Platform with RGB light fixture.

steps.title: Inoculate bacteria overnight
steps.instruction: Inoculate each bacterial isolate in 5 mL FMAP medium inside 15 mL culture tubes and place on the shaker to shake overnight.

steps.title: Prepare IAA stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1H‑Indole‑3‑acetic acid (98 %, CAS 87‑51‑4) in Milli‑Q water to a final concentration of 0.25 mM. Wrap the container in aluminum foil and store short‑term in a refrigerator; for long‑term storage keep at –20 °C.

steps.title: Acclimate bacteria to cold room
steps.instruction: Transfer the overnight bacterial culture tubes to the 7 °C cold‑room and let them acclimate overnight.

steps.title: Prepare sodium metasilicate stock
steps.instruction: Make a 3.5 g L⁻¹ sodium metasilicate solution (CAS 6834‑92‑0) in Milli‑Q water.

steps.title: Prepare fresh culture media
steps.instruction: To 5 L of filtered seawater add 8 mg mL⁻¹ Guillard’s (F/2) Marine Water Enrichment Solution (50×) and 8 mg mL⁻¹ of the 3.5 g L⁻¹ sodium metasilicate stock. This volume supplies nine 500 mL tissue‑culture flasks (3 treatments × 3 replicates).

steps.title: Filter media and fill flasks
steps.instruction: Filter the prepared media through 0.22 µm sterile Sterivex pressure filters using a Masterflex L/S peristaltic pump, then dispense into nine 500 mL tissue‑culture flasks, ensuring not to exceed filter capacity.

steps.title: Dilute algae culture to target density
steps.instruction: Dilute the stock diatom culture with Milli‑Q water to achieve a starting concentration of 1–2 × 10⁶ cells L⁻¹ (approximately a 1:3 dilution of the original culture).

steps.title: Transfer diatoms to culture flasks
steps.instruction: Add the diluted diatom suspension to each 500 mL flask to reach the target cell density.

steps.title: Add bacteria to achieve 50:1 ratio
steps.instruction: Measure the optical density at 600 nm (OD₆₀₀) of each bacterial isolate, calculate the volume needed for a 50 : 1 bacteria‑to‑diatom ratio, and pipette the appropriate amount into each flask.

steps.title: Homogenize cultures and set shaker
steps.instruction: Turn each flask over ten times to homogenize, place them on the orbital shaker in the 7 °C cold‑room, set shaker to 50 rpm, 300 reciprocal motions for 12 s, vibration level 2, and verify uniform light intensity; alternate bottle positions.

steps.title: Collect 25 mL samples for analysis
steps.instruction: From each culture flask withdraw 25 mL into a 50 mL Falcon tube, immediately return the flask to the shaker; allocate 4 mL for cell counting and 20 mL for chlorophyll extraction.

steps.title: Count diatom cells using Utermöhl method
steps.instruction: From each 25 mL sample pipette two 2 mL aliquots into 2 mL cell‑culture wells, add 7 µL Lugol’s iodine solution to each, incubate 1–2 h at 4 °C, then examine under a microscope. Count cells in duplicate wells horizontally (excluding bottom edge) and vertically (excluding right edge); average the four counts to obtain cells L⁻¹.

steps.title: Filter remaining sample for chlorophyll extraction
steps.instruction: Using a vacuum pump with a 1.2 µm GF/C glass‑microfiber filter, divide the remaining 21 mL of each sample into five 4 mL aliquots and filter each onto a separate filter (technical replicates).

steps.title: Extract chlorophyll from filters
steps.instruction: Transfer each filter to a separate test tube, add 5 mL 96–100 % ethanol, cover with foil, and store overnight at 7 °C.

steps.title: Measure chlorophyll a fluorescence
steps.instruction: After extraction, measure chlorophyll a on a TD‑700 fluorometer (excitation 430–450 nm, emission 675–685 nm). Convert absorbance to concentration using a factor of 0.00417 µg L⁻¹ per absorbance unit.
